title: Oak: Ancient Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Old oaks whose exact species nobody has confirmed. Lukavice's oak in Bohemia, nearly 800 years old, was voted Czech Tree of the Year in 2024.
intro: These oaks carry only their genus, Quercus, because nobody has yet taken a leaf or an acorn stalk close enough to say which species each one is. That gap does not make them less worth the walk. The oak on the Hrádek at Lukavice, put at nearly 800 years, survived an estate manager stripping cartloads of soil from its roots and was voted Czech Tree of the Year in 2024. Belfast's Belvoir Oak got down to six acorns one winter and is still standing. Ypres's Christusboom has been cut to nothing by two wars and grown back from the stump both times. Austin's Auction Oaks shaded the 1839 sale of town lots before the city existed. Hainich's Betteleiche is hollow because medieval friars are said to have carved it out to keep alms dry. If you can tell a pedunculate from a sessile oak at a glance, tell us.
